rule: When deprecating a Python dependency, update DEPRECATED_PACKAGES in homeassistant/requirements.py and the FORBIDDEN_PACKAGES entry in script/hassfest/requirements.py together, including the replacement package named in the reason text.
trigger: A change to the DEPRECATED_PACKAGES dict in homeassistant/requirements.py with no matching change to FORBIDDEN_PACKAGES in script/hassfest/requirements.py.
rationale: The two lists express the same deprecation to different audiences; leaving hassfest pointing at the old replacement means new integrations are steered to a package that is itself deprecated.

evidence.excerpt: pyserial-asyncio-fast should be added to FORBIDDEN_PACKAGES since it is also now deprecated

rule: Keep the pylint plugin README's description of a checker's accepted and rejected patterns exactly in step with the checker implementation and its test cases.
trigger: A change to pylint/plugins/README.md or a checker module docstring describing which code shapes the checker accepts, without a matching implementation or test in pylint/plugins/pylint_home_assistant/checkers/.
rationale: The README is what contributors consult when a custom check fires; documenting a guard form as rejected when the checker actually accepts it sends people to work around a rule that does not exist.

evidence.excerpt: The README documentation incorrectly states that raise guards break the guarantee

rule: Custom pylint checkers that recognise service registrations must handle the service_func= keyword form as well as the positional argument, for both async_register and async_register_admin_service.
trigger: A checker helper in pylint/plugins that extracts a handler from hass.services.async_register / async_register_admin_service using only call.args positional indexes.
rationale: Several integrations register actions with the keyword form, so a positional-only matcher silently skips their handlers and the check never runs where it matters.

evidence.excerpt: Handle service_func= keyword registrations here; several integrations register services this way

rule: Narrow custom pylint checks so they fire only on the exact pattern they target; a check on exception construction must require a literal string or f-string message, not merely the presence of a positional argument.
trigger: A checker condition of the form `if node.args and not has_translation_key` (or similar) that inspects only argument count rather than the argument node type.
rationale: Broad conditions flag idiomatic code such as `raise ConfigEntryAuthFailed(err) from err`, generating false positives across the tree and forcing widespread pylint disable comments.

evidence.excerpt: Refine the W7417 check to only trigger when a positional string message is provided

rule: Keep file-glob constants in script/ tooling identical to the paths: filter of the GitHub workflow that invokes them.
trigger: A TRACKED_PATTERNS-style glob tuple in script/ that is narrower than the paths: filter of the corresponding .github/workflows/*.yml.
rationale: The workflow triggers on a broader pattern than the script matches, so files that started the run are ignored by the diff parser and the check passes without examining them.

evidence.excerpt: Align the tracked file patterns with the deterministic workflow's paths filter

rule: New hassfest validation must ship with hassfest tests exercising both the valid case and each distinct failure mode it can report.
trigger: A new validation branch in script/hassfest/*.py that adds an error message, with no corresponding case added under tests/hassfest/.
rationale: Hassfest errors gate every integration PR, so validation that is never exercised can reject correct manifests or silently stop validating after a refactor.

evidence.excerpt: Add hassfest tests that cover valid and invalid context usage

rule: When a config flow gains a fallback path, add a test for its success case end to end, not only for the error case that motivated it.
trigger: A new branch in an integration's config_flow.py that calls the client on a cache miss, with test_config_flow.py changes covering only the failure outcome.
rationale: Config flow branches are the code users hit first; an untested success path means the new fallback can be broken end to end while the suite stays green.

evidence.excerpt: Add a test that covers the success path where the selected model

rule: When a platform converts raw API values into device_class or state_class enums, add a test feeding a missing or invalid value and assert setup does not raise and the entity is still created with the attribute unset.
trigger: New SensorDeviceClass/SensorStateClass enum lookups on payload data in an integration's sensor.py, with tests covering only well-formed payloads.
rationale: Device payloads omit or misspell these fields in the wild; an unguarded enum conversion takes down entity creation for the whole device.

evidence.excerpt: Add a test case that feeds a message producing a reading with state_class=None

rule: Do not assert exact library call counts during setup; assert the resulting device and entity registry state instead.
trigger: An assertion of the form `assert mock_client.<method>.call_count == N` in an integration test covering config entry setup.
rationale: Call counts encode internal polling and refresh details, so any change to setup ordering breaks tests that are not actually about the behaviour under test.

evidence.excerpt: Avoid asserting an exact get_bluetooth_remotes.call_count during setup; validate behavior via the device/entity registry

rule: Test module and test function docstrings must name the platform and behaviour actually under test; update them when the parametrization or the file's subject changes.
trigger: A new or copied test file whose module docstring names a different platform than the file tests, or a parametrized test whose docstring describes only a subset of the cases in its params list.
rationale: The docstring is what a reader sees first in a failure report, so a copy-pasted or stale one misdirects whoever is triaging the failure.

evidence.excerpt: The test file docstring incorrectly says Tests for the Cambridge Audio select platform
this parametrized test also covers counter.incremented/counter.decremented, which are direction-based transitions
Updating the docstring would avoid confusion when reading failures.

rule: Drive a test's expected end state with a realistic mock sequence (raise once, then return data) rather than an always-raising mock that reaches the expected state only through internal retry or swallowing.
trigger: A test parametrized over ConfigEntryState.LOADED whose client mock has an unconditional side_effect exception on the data-fetch method.
rationale: An always-failing mock makes the loaded case depend on internal swallow/retry behaviour instead of a successful fetch, so the test passes for the wrong reason and stops protecting the reauth path.

evidence.excerpt: Consider using a sequential side_effect that raises once and then returns valid data

rule: Use the integration's DOMAIN constant wherever the domain appears, including as the key of the configuration dict passed to async_setup_component, rather than repeating the domain string.
trigger: A hardcoded domain string in a test or component module that already imports DOMAIN, e.g. async_setup_component(hass, DOMAIN, {"counter": {...}}).
rationale: Mixing the constant and the literal in the same call leaves half the references unprotected against a domain rename and reads as an oversight in a PR whose whole point was to use the constant.

evidence.excerpt: The configuration dictionary key should also use the DOMAIN constant instead of the hardcoded string

rule: Do not stack repeated await hass.async_block_till_done() calls to make a fixture settle; use a single deterministic wait or document why more than one pass is required.
trigger: Two or more consecutive `await hass.async_block_till_done()` statements in a test or conftest fixture.
rationale: Repeated passes paper over a scheduling or race problem in setup rather than exposing it, so the test keeps passing while the underlying ordering bug stays hidden.

evidence.excerpt: Replace the repeated async_block_till_done() calls with a single deterministic wait

rule: Mock an integration's library with AsyncMock-based fixtures rather than hand-written fake client classes.
trigger: A new conftest.py defining a stub class that reimplements the vendor library's properties and setters instead of patching the client with AsyncMock.
rationale: Fake classes look tidy at first but accumulate customization as tests grow; existing integrations such as niko_home_control show the AsyncMock fixture shape reviewers expect.

evidence.excerpt: not a big fan of mock classes; I prefer AsyncMocks way more nowadays

rule: When core code branches on whether the caller is a built-in integration (module starting with homeassistant.components.), test both the warning branch and the suppression branch.
trigger: A new report/warning in homeassistant/ that is skipped for modules under homeassistant.components., with tests asserting only the warning case.
rationale: Without coverage of the suppression branch a later change silently reintroduces startup warnings from core integrations, which is exactly what the branch exists to prevent.

evidence.excerpt: Add test coverage for the branch that suppresses the warning for built-in integrations
